newsitem.title: FRANCE: Finland backs Baltic states' right to join NATO.
newsitem.headline: Finland backs Baltic states' right to join NATO.

text.p: The president of neutral Finland, Martti Ahtisaari, on Tuesday defended the right of the neighbouring Baltic states to join NATO despite Russia's opposition.

Ahtisaari told the parliamentary assembly of the Western European Union that every country, including the Baltic states, had a basic right to decide its own security. No country should be left outside an enlarged NATO against its will.

"It is of particular importance that the security needs of the Baltic states be taken into account...We support their right to apply for membership of NATO," he told the European defence body's Paris-based assembly.

"It is absolutely vital that we recognise the right of each country to decide on its defence policy. We support the right of the Baltic and central European states to make their own choice," he later told a news conference.

The Baltic states of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia, which regained their independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991, are all eager to enter NATO as they seek to make sure they never again come under the rule of Moscow.

Russia last month signed a partnership agreement with NATO, tacitly accepting it could not prevent the alliance from expanding to include former communist countries in Eastern Europe. But it vociferously opposes membership for the Baltics, which it says would call into question its whole relationship with the West.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic lead the field of 11 countries wanting to become the first new members of the West's military alliance since Spain in 1982.
Ahtisaari also backed the Baltic states' future membership of the European Union, which Finland joined in 1995.

"Enlargement of the Union is an essential part of the region's future. It must also be part of the future of the Baltic states, which have made admirable progress on their road back to Europe," he said.
